issues.explanation: callNext() never validates the public mode property and uses CallMode::tryFrom(...) ?? CallMode::Any, so an invalid or tampered mode silently becomes any and can still call a ticket instead of being rejected as the task's CallMode::from($mode) and the Livewire validation policy require.

The suites prove mount-level denial and foreign-id handling, but there is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for create, startRename, rename, toggleActive or revokeAccess, which the project's Livewire test policy requires for each action.

render() trusts the client-writable viewingQueueId, accessQueueId and managingAccess and renders the queue detail and access grants without re-checking update/manageAccess, so setting those properties directly bypasses the checks performed by openQueue()/openAccess() for same-entity queues.
Using 0 as a fallback id turns the no-queue-selected case into a confusing ModelNotFoundException; an explicit guard or a helper that resolves the viewed/edited queue would read better.
The new public component methods have no PHPDoc even though the project's docs convention asks for PHPDoc on public methods (the properties are documented, the methods are not).

review.summary: Adds the queues management and attendant serve Livewire pages, members tabs, navbar links, translations, docs and a substantial Pest suite, with every client id resolved against the current entity and domain writes delegated to the existing actions. The main flow is complete and well tested, but mode is not validated and silently falls back to any instead of CallMode::from, some per-action unauthorized/tamper tests are missing, and render() trusts a few client-writable state properties; these are fixable nits rather than blockers.
